Where it began

Hasan Ali was born on 2 July 1994 in Ladhe Wala Waraich, a village near Gujranwala in Punjab. His family encouraged his cricket from the start. Proper coaching started when he was ten, under Ansar Zafar Rathore at his Young Combine Star Club, the same Gujranwala club where the international cricketer Imran Nazir trained. He was a devoted trainer, and by fourteen he had been picked for the city's junior side.

The player

His first one-day international came against Ireland in August 2016, and in May 2017 he won his first Test cap, in the third match of a series in the West Indies. A month later came the summer that made his name. At the 2017 Champions Trophy he took 13 wickets, equalling the record at the time for a single edition, and was named player of the tournament as Pakistan won it for the first time, beating India by 180 runs in the final.

That year he took more one-day wickets than anyone, 45 in all and became the quickest Pakistani to 50 one-day wickets. In Tests, by November 2026 he had played 27 matches and taken 88 wickets at 28.09, with six five-wicket hauls, a best of 5 for 27 and one ten-wicket match.

What made him special

Wickets, and fast. Just 426 days after his international debut he was ranked the best one-day bowler in the world, one of the quickest climbs anyone had made. He was later the Pakistan board's Test Cricketer of the Year for 2021 and was named in the world Test team of that year.

His Test batting was more about entertainment than accumulation, with a top score of 30. Yet in January 2021 he hit a century in the final of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy and was named player of the match and of the tournament, so the runs were in there somewhere.

Away from the middle

He was a regular in Twenty20 leagues. No one took more wickets in the 2019 Pakistan Super League than his twenty-five, and he was named its Bowler of the Tournament. He played for Peshawar Zalmi, Islamabad United and Karachi Kings, and in 2025 the Adelaide Strikers picked him in their draft for Australia's Big Bash League. In England he spent part of the 2022 season with Lancashire. He was also named the world's Emerging Cricketer of the Year for 2017.

And finally

Plenty of fast bowlers dream of a hundred in a final. Hasan Ali actually made one, which must have made for a lively dressing room every time the batsmen complained about the bowlers.
